scenes.headline: You already know the sign rule
scenes.caption: Your diagnostic showed this signed multiplication correctly.

scenes.headline: Write two signed products
scenes.caption: The outside negative two multiplies both signed terms.

scenes.headline: Now apply the rule you know
scenes.caption: Negative two times negative five becomes positive ten.

scenes.headline: Signs first. Arithmetic second.
scenes.caption: Write both products before calculating whenever a negative sits outside.

scenes.headline: The fraction was not the problem
scenes.caption: You correctly distributed one half across the first bracket.

scenes.headline: Three must reach both terms
scenes.caption: Use one visible arrow for each term inside the bracket.

scenes.headline: Combine only after both brackets open
scenes.caption: Open every bracket completely before combining like terms.

scenes.headline: Count terms; count products
scenes.caption: Two terms inside a bracket require two multiplications.

scenes.headline: Your algebraic route worked
scenes.caption: Your expansion and balance steps were correct.

scenes.headline: Try your answer in the original
scenes.caption: Substitution reveals that the final arithmetic needs another look.

scenes.headline: Thirty-three divided by three
scenes.caption: Eleven returns twenty-one in the original equation.

scenes.headline: Solve, substitute, confirm
scenes.caption: Keep your algebraic method and add this quick final check.

scenes.headline: You combined the x terms correctly
scenes.caption: The remaining step is about preserving equality.

scenes.headline: Cancel negative six with positive six
scenes.caption: The equals sign requires the same addition on both sides.

scenes.headline: Both sides stayed equal
scenes.caption: The balanced equation now gives x equals seven.

scenes.headline: Name it on both sides
scenes.caption: Write the operation on both sides until the habit is secure.

lessons.title: A fresh start: show one step at a time

scenes.headline: Cogna needs clearer evidence
scenes.caption: Sparse or conflicting evidence cannot support an academic gap claim.

scenes.headline: Write the first useful step
scenes.caption: One working step helps separate a method from a guess.

scenes.headline: Not knowing is useful evidence
scenes.caption: Choose the response that describes your current state.

scenes.headline: Two clean questions—then Cogna decides
scenes.caption: Cogna concludes only when fresh evidence supports a conclusion.
